edit.description: `waveWall` hands back the wall it did not class; `settledWaveVerdict` puts it on the verdict beside the class
the verdict's home for the unclassed wall, alongside the existing optional-failure family
the same fact on `TickResult`, as every sibling failure bucket already is
the two-wall case asserts both walls, and its slot-leg vacuity reads the reported fact rather than a missing row

summary: A wave holding two walls reports only the ranked one: the loser's cause reaches no verdict field, no `TickResult`, and no log line

per.section: A fact the engine holds is reported, never rediscovered

acceptance: A fanout wave that hits both walls reports both: `waveWall`'s ranking still decides the class, the exit arm and the summary, and the wall it did not class rides the verdict and `TickResult` as a fact beside it. A wave holding one wall reports exactly what it reports today.
tests: a wave holding a refused ledger rewrite and a slot leg's throw reports both walls on its verdict
the wall a wave's ranking did not class rides the TickResult beside the class it did
notes: `waveWall` (`src/waveMerge.ts:1174`) returns one `cause`/`event` and the losing holder is dropped there. Nothing else records it: `slotError ??=` (`src/waveTick.ts:662`, `:674`) has no `log.warn` beside it, and none of the verdict's seven `*Failures` buckets has an arm for a slot-leg throw, so the summary (`:1276`) names the ranked wall alone. A fact, never a verdict — what a second wall means stays the chain's. Lever: a thrown teardown beside a pick whose rewrite read an unparseable queue.
